title: Tormach post: G53 G0 Z0 retract assumes machine Z0 is the top of travel - a LinuxCNC machine homed at the bottom drives into the part

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Reported on #435 by @tbrasselle: the built-in Tormach PathPilot post (v0.14.0, same on main) was used to drive a LinuxCNC machine. The program had to be hand-edited before it was safe to run:

> I had to remove the G30 Z0 lines from beginning and end of the toolpath. My machine has Z0 set to the tool all the way down. this would have driven the spindle and tool into the workpiece rather than up and away as it was intended.

The post retracts with `G53 G0 Z0`, followed by `G30`, before every tool change (`startPreamble`) and at the program end (`onClose`). That is correct on a Tormach, where machine Z home is the top of travel. On a LinuxCNC machine homed with machine Z0 at the bottom, `G53 G0 Z0` is a rapid **down** to the bottom of travel, through the part. Nothing in the post or the gate catches this: the move is in machine coordinates, so the program sim and the stroke check never see it.

A crash, not a gouge, so P1 rather than P0: the post is named for Tormach, and on a Tormach the output is right. But PathPilot is LinuxCNC, so using this post on another LinuxCNC machine is an obvious thing to try.

Options (for discussion):
1. Take the safe-retract Z from the machine file: a `.mch` key for "Z top of travel in machine coordinates", 0 for the Tormach machines. When the document's machine doesn't state one, refuse to post by name rather than guess.
2. Add a generic LinuxCNC post whose retract is `G91 G0 Z<clearance>` / `G90`, or `G53 G0 Z<stated top>` from the machine file, and leave the Tormach post Tormach-only.
3. State in the posted header comment which convention the retract assumes (for example "machine Z0 = top of travel (Tormach)").

Done means: a program posted for a machine whose Z home is not machine Z0 never emits a rapid to machine Z0, or posting is refused by name, pinned by a test.
